ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B = \angle C$. Point $D$ is on side $AB$. A line is drawn through $D$, with $DE \perp BC$ intersecting $BC$ at point $E$ and extending to intersect the extended line of $CA$ at point $F$. Given $AC = 5$ and $BD = 3$, what is the length of $AF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $DE\perp BC$,\\
it follows that $\angle DEB=\angle FEC=90^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle B+\angle BDE=90^\circ$, $\angle C+\angle F=90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle B=\angle C$,\\
it results in $\angle F=\angle BDE$,\\
and since $\angle FDA=\angle BDE$,\\
we have $\angle FDA=\angle F$,\\
hence $AF=AD$,\\
as $\angle B=\angle C$ and $AC=5$,\\
it implies $AB=AC=5$,\\
given $BD=3$,\\
it follows $AD=AB−BD=5−3=2$,\\
thus $AF=AD=\boxed{2}$.
